According to the Bohr-Bury rule (or the rule) for the filling of electrons in multi-electron atoms:

  • Orbitals with a lower value of have lower energy.

Therefore, Statement A is true.

Statement B: Energies of the orbitals in the same subshell increase with increase in atomic number.

As the atomic number () increases, the nuclear charge increases. This leads to a stronger electrostatic pull on the electrons by the nucleus, which increases the effective nuclear charge (). Due to this stronger attraction, the electrons are held more tightly, and the energy of the orbitals becomes more negative (it decreases, not increases).
